# `Q-9-13` — Circular Macro Dependency

> CSL macro references form a cycle: macro A invokes B, B
> invokes A (directly or transitively).

## What this means

CSL macros call each other through `<cs:text macro="...">`. The
parser builds a call graph and requires it to be acyclic — a
macro that ultimately depends on itself can never finish
rendering. This error fires when the parser detects a cycle.
The message includes the cycle itself, as a chain of macro
names connected by `->`.

## Why this happens

Two common causes:

- **An author refactor** that introduced a circular call by
  accident — renaming a macro and updating some but not all
  callers, or splitting one macro into two that reference each
  other.
- **A hand-translated style** from a different citation
  framework where the equivalent recursion was allowed.

## How to fix

Break the cycle. The message shows the cycle as a chain of
names: pick the edge that does not need to be a macro call and
inline its content, or rework the design so that no macro
needs to invoke a transitive ancestor.

## Related

- `Q-9-12` — undefined macro: a different macro-reference
  problem, where the called name does not exist at all.
